items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: he taught all the drummers, his name was George Peterson

ctx.x: Well, you mentioned the mutes. When did mutes become, what kind of mutes were really popular? Straight mutes. Straight mutes?

Yeah. There was a, Mr. Peterson who was the dean of all the drummers, he taught all the drummers, his name was George Peterson, he used to make them out of fiber. Out of what? Fiber, some kind of fiber. Red. Fiber? Oh, I call it fiber. It's a stiff material. It's a cardboard. And I invented a lot of mutes but I failed to have them copyrighted. But the Dixie Music Company in Chicago had them copyrighted. I invented the cup mute. I used to have a large Salisbury can attached to a straight mute. And when I played…
